name: foundry-packages
description: Workspace root. Not published — see packages/ for the published packages.

scripts.//shell: npm runs these with /bin/sh, which is dash on most Linux CI images and has no arrays and no shopt. They must be POSIX. An unmatched glob expands to the literal pattern, so `[ -d ]` on the first word is the portable way to ask whether packages/ has anything in it.
scripts.//build-order: npm --workspaces builds in filesystem-discovery order, not dependency order. Build the dependency roots first: controller has no first-party dependency of its own and is what builder, inspector and ledger now resolve through; ui must exist before surface compiles its web templates and token consumers; and locksmith has an internal subpath that must build on a fresh clone. The governance and policy stubs that issue #282 introduced as forwarding shims are gone -- their only remaining consumers were repointed at controller directly, because a stub kept for its own sake is the debt decision 9 exists to remove.
scripts.build: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run build --workspace=packages/controller --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/designer --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/writer --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/locksmith --if-present && npm run build --workspaces --if-present
scripts.test: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run test --workspaces --if-present
scripts.typecheck: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present
scripts.//check-registry: Does every non-private packages/*/package.json's publishConfig.registry still match the single declared registry in package-scope.json? Same single-source-of-truth pattern as check:scope, extended from the scope to the registry -- see scripts/set-registry.mjs's own header and docs/PUBLISHING.md's canonical registry qualification section.
scripts.//check-prepublish-hook: Does every non-private packages/*/package.json's scripts.prepublishOnly still run check-name-collision.mjs before npm run build? Same single-source-of-truth pattern as check:scope and check:registry above -- see scripts/set-prepublish-hook.mjs's own header for why this closes issue #273's hand-run `npm publish` bypass, and why it does not (and cannot) claim to close every bypass.
scripts.//check-gates: The fixture-driven gate regression suite, plus every node:test suite over this repository's own scripts. One entry is deliberately not under scripts/: `.github/scripts/collect-credential-evidence.test.mjs`, which covers the collector ci.yml's `credential lifecycle` job actually runs. It belongs HERE rather than in check:verify-inputs -- the other .github/scripts suite -- because the two have opposite needs. That one runs the real assembler and the real compiled inspector bin, so it must sit after `npm run build`; this one imports only collect-credential-evidence.mjs's exported YAML/timestamp parsers, and that module reaches node builtins plus scripts/lib/gh-api.mjs (builtins-only) and nothing else, so it needs nothing compiled and nothing installed. That is the same condition every other entry here already meets, and it is what lets this whole compound run in ci.yml's dependency-free `safety` job, before anything is built. Importing the collector makes no Jobs API call: its module body is inert, self-invoking only under `process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`. Adding a suite to this list is the whole wiring -- ci.yml invokes `npm run check:gates` by name, never by path list, so a new suite needs no CI step of its own.
scripts.//check-foreign-references: The inverse of check:safety. That gate is a denylist and can only refuse names someone already listed; this one allows only THIS repository's own account and scope (derived from package-scope.json and the manifests' own repository.url) and fails every other account-shaped reference by shape. Foundry is a neutral supplier: it must never name a consumer, a sibling repository, or any other account. See the script's own header for the leak that got past check:safety and motivated it.
scripts.//check-workspace-links: Does every first-party 0.x dependency range still cover its sibling's real on-disk version, and does package-lock.json still resolve every first-party package as a local link rather than a remote registry URL? See the script's own header for the defect this exists to catch -- it has already cost real time more than once.
scripts.//check-lock-workspace-versions: Does package-lock.json's own "packages/<dir>": { "version": ... } record for every packages/*/package.json still match that manifest's real, on-disk version (issue #917)? Package set is derived from packages/* on disk, never a hand-written list (issue #907's rule). A fresh `npm ci` resolves workspace versions FROM the lock, so a stale entry is a lie `npm ci` trusts. Pre-existing drift at the time this gate landed is recorded once in governance/known-lock-version-drift.json, keyed to #917 and pinned to the exact lock/manifest pair observed -- a self-cleaning ratchet, same pattern as governance/known-dangling-citations.json and check-contamination-classes.mjs: a pin that stops matching current drift is itself a finding. Deliberately does NOT touch check:qualification-record-required's rootPackageLockSha256 pin, which resolves against a pre-publication record's own reviewedCommit and is unaffected by a later lock change on main -- see the script's own header.

scripts.//check-visibility-declarations: The OFFLINE half of check:package-visibility, split out so it can run on every pull request. That gate calls the live public npm registry over the network, so it only runs on schedule -- see package-visibility.yml -- not because it needs a credential (it needs none). This half needs no network access at all: it confirms governance/release-catalog.json's active release target actually resolves against package-scope.json, and that every "deprecated" package under the active scope declares a valid, unexpired docs/contracts/package-retention.json entry. This half is a real gate; the live half stays out of `check` only because it is a network call.
scripts.//check-first-wave-sequence: Is the committed first-wave productization order still a topological order of first-party runtime edges, still Advisor -> Starter -> Controller, still operational integrity ahead of expression, and still publisher before influencer? Distinct from the release-catalogue upload order, which places writer and designer early only because publisher cannot publish without them. See docs/FIRST-WAVE.md and docs/DECISIONS.md decision 27.
scripts.//check-install-docs: Does any current-scope package README tell a consumer they need a GitHub token or GitHub Packages to install this package? The #924 class. Missing public-npm install claims are printed and counted, never a failure. README text only, so it runs before build alongside the other declaration gates.
scripts.//check-conversation-contract: Composes every packages/*/skill/SKILL.md source the way @clossys/launcher does (replacing its own `## How we work together` / `## One question at a time` sections with docs/contracts/conversation-contract.md, #1182) into a temp directory, and asserts the current contract appears exactly once with no leftover legacy heading. Reads source files only, so it runs before build alongside the other declaration gates; its own regression suite is in check:gates.
scripts.//check-bin-reachability: Does every declared packages/*/package.json bin produce output when invoked through a fresh node_modules/.bin-shaped symlink (#909)? Needs compiled dist/, so it lives after npm run build, never in check:gates. Fixture tests of the gate live in check:gates.
scripts.//check-role-assessment-surfaces: Does every role package that DECLARES a first-day assessment entry point (foundry.assessment) actually map that bin in its own manifest? The onboarding workflow in @clossys/controller/onboarding discovers a role assessment only from that declaration and never infers one, so a declaration naming an unmapped bin reads as wired to its author and as absent to the discovery code. Advisor, the engagement-gate role, must declare one: an undeclared Advisor is a finding, not a counted gap. The gate also always prints the roles that declare no surface at all, and their count: those are not a failure, but a capability requiring zero targets must not grade identically to one fully covered (issue #435), and a number allowed to stay invisible is a number allowed to stay wrong. Manifest-only, so it runs before build alongside the other declaration gates.
scripts.//check-package-framework: docs/contracts/package-framework.json extends the manifest foundry block (assessment already existed) with intake, outputs, status, and fit; docs/contracts/check-output-envelope.json and docs/contracts/role-assessment.json give the check-run and role-assessment-document shapes those surfaces feed (issue #1174). Report mode: prints a conformance table for every active role and fails only when a field a package DOES declare is malformed -- absence is printed and counted, never a failure, until --enforce (a later wave). Manifest- and fixture-read only, so it runs before build alongside the other declaration gates.
scripts.//check-capability-maps: docs/contracts/package-framework.json version 3 adds foundry.capabilities (issue #1196): a MECE capability map per role, checked within a role (no two capabilities share an output, sub-questions distinct) and, under --enforce, across every role (every output has exactly one owner, every feeds entry is produced by exactly one capability). Report mode: absence is printed and counted, never a failure, until the per-role maps (#1198-#1202) land and --enforce turns on. Manifest-read only, so it runs before build alongside the other declaration gates.
scripts.//check-package-conformance: The Stage B normalization-template gate (issue #1187's normalization direction; issue #1203's scaffold and issue #1197's loop matrix are its siblings): for every package under packages/, reports each gap against the Stage A shared definitions (manifest block, output envelope, lifecycle words, generated loop section, clossys/<role>/ layout, removed conversation duplicate, capability map, STATUS.md shape). Report mode by default; --enforce for the later wave once Stage C conversion completes. Manifest-, contract-, and fixture-read only, no build.
scripts.//check-loop-matrix: Issue #1197: validates each active role's own packages/<pkg>/loop-matrix.json (docs/contracts/loop-matrix.json) and fails when a committed "Run the feedback loop" skill section has drifted from what scripts/generate-loop-section.mjs generates from it -- always, in both modes. Absence of the matrix itself is report-mode-only until --enforce.
scripts.//scaffold-package: Issue #1203: generates a new role package already conforming to check:package-conformance, for a role docs/contracts/role-loop-archetypes.json already declares. Usage: node scripts/scaffold-package.mjs <role-short-name>.
scripts.//check-verify-inputs: The collector half of this repository's own verify-standards run: does .github/scripts/assemble-verify-inputs.mjs still aim a work-item lookup at the repository the reference NAMES, and does the built CLI still refuse what it could not aim there? Both halves, because a collector that reports the right thing and a decision that ignores it is still a false pass (issue #363). Runs the real script and the real bin.js, so it needs `npm run build` first and lives after it in the chain -- not in check:gates, which runs before anything is compiled.
scripts.check:readme: node scripts/check-root-readme-parity.mjs . && for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-readme-parity.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.check:contamination: for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-contamination-classes.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.check:typechecked-assertions: for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-typechecked-assertions.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.//check:readme-examples: Needs each package's own dist/ (its shipped declarations) -- run after npm run build, not before.
scripts.check:readme-examples: for manifest in packages/*/package.json; do [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue; p=${manifest%/package.json}; node scripts/check-readme-examples.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.//check-repository-profile: Foundry supplies the repository-requirements contract and, per issue #317, declares and verifies its own governance/repository-profile.json rather than being the one repository that skips it. Invoked with `.` (the repository root), not an explicit file path, so this also exercises the packaged discovery repository-check gained in issue #315: it must locate governance/repository-profile.json itself, and a declaration anywhere else would surface as a distinct, non-canonical-location finding rather than a silent pass. `bin.js`, not `cli.js`, the same executable-only entry point `repository-check` installs as -- controller/repository's own CLI module is deliberately inert on import (see its own header), so only bin.js self-invokes.
scripts.//check-locksmith-catalog: Foundry's own value-free credential catalogue names the workflow credential classes this repository actually requires, never their values. Run the built locksmith CLI by its dist path after `npm run build`; this is author-side staging evidence, not a provider connection or consumer adoption (#494, #496).
scripts.//check-launcher-help: Launcher get-started help, invoked by dist path after `npm run build`. The script exists so package-evidence has a packages/launcher/dist site — the bin name `launcher` would otherwise fire invocation-by-bin-name against a clone that cites the package but has no dist-path site. Needs compiled dist/; keep out of check:gates. Wired into ci.yml's post-build job (#414).
scripts.//check-strategist-subject: Foundry's wired strategist facts subject (clossys/strategist/facts.json) traced against docs/PUBLISHING.md only. Invoked by packages/strategist/dist/cli.js after build; wired into ci.yml's post-build job (#500).
scripts.//check-supersession: Foundry's public, repository-owned donor map is evaluated against this repository's own root manifest through integrator's built CLI. It is deliberately outside publish.yml's bootstrap discovery, which runs before node_modules and dist exist (#495, #496).
scripts.//check-contrast: designer-contrast-check ships as an installed `bin` (packages/designer/src/tokens/contrast-cli.ts), but a gate nothing ever runs is decorative — invoked here directly against designer’s own compiled dist/tokens/contrast-cli.js, the same way check:package-governance below invokes controller’s own dist/cli.js, rather than via `npx` or a workspace script indirection. Needs `npm run build` (designer’s own `dist/` is gitignored) to have run first, same as check:package-governance. REPOINTED from packages/ui when the five expression donors were removed (#469). The move is coverage-neutral and was proven rather than assumed: the two packages shipped byte-identical CONTRAST_PAIRS and tokens.css files differing only in a header comment, and the repointed CLI fed a tokens.css with --color-ink-primary set equal to --color-surface-base exits 1 with three light-theme findings. The CI job deliberately KEEPS the name “WCAG contrast gate (ui-contrast-check)” even though it no longer runs ui’s copy: that exact string is a required status check on main, and renaming a required context is a three-phase operation rather than a rename.
scripts.//check-neutrality: The structural half of publish safety, for material meant to be shared between parties who do not govern each other: an absolute path or a named home directory discloses one operator's machine layout without containing a single denylisted string, so check:safety can never see it. Runs the BUILT @clossys/controller/conventions scan (issue #282 moved this off the now-retired @example/conventions) rather than a second copy of those regexes here — hence its position after build, alongside check:package-governance and check:contrast.
scripts.//check-release-readiness: Did a package's shipped content change since its version last did, scoped to the diff against origin/main (or local main)? Offline and hermetic (see scripts/check-release-readiness.test.mjs) — no network call, just local git refs — but deliberately NOT part of `check` below: its answer is only as fresh as the contributor's local origin/main, which `git fetch` keeps current but `check`'s other gates never depend on being current for anything. Run explicitly, or trust CI's `release-readiness` job, which passes the pull request's real base explicitly rather than relying on a local ref at all. A separate `--audit` mode also exists for whole-repo, non-diff-scoped investigation — see the script's own header for why that mode is a heuristic and is not run in CI.
scripts.//check-qualification-record-required: For any package whose version changed relative to origin/main (or local main), does the new version already have a retained, matching qualification record — or an acknowledged, issue-referenced deferral in governance/release-qualification-deferrals.json? Reuses check-release-readiness.mjs's own merge-base computation and check-qualification-record-present.mjs's own present/missing/stale join (issue #863). Same reason as check:release-readiness immediately above for staying OUT of `check` below: its answer is only as fresh as the contributor's local origin/main. Run explicitly, or trust CI's `qualification-record-required` job, which passes the pull request's real base explicitly.
scripts.//check-builds-first: build runs before typecheck for the same reason ci.yml does it in that order: dist/ is gitignored, so on a fresh clone a package's internal dependency has no .d.ts until it has been compiled. The explicit pre-build list exists because `npm run build --workspaces` iterates alphabetically, not topologically: a package that sorts BEFORE a first-party dependency compiles against declarations that do not exist yet. ui is listed because surface sorts before it; designer and writer are listed because publisher sorts before writer. This list must grow whenever a new package sorts before something it depends on, and a local tree with stale dist/ output will not reveal the omission -- only a fresh clone will.

scripts.//preflight: Everything a package must pass before a publish is even proposed. Unlike `check`, this scans the packed TARBALL and asks the registry whether the name is already taken.
scripts.//publish-plan: Read-only (issue #1227): lists every non-private package, whether it would publish, and why the rest would not -- "on npm already" and "qualification record missing/stale" are kept as distinct reasons. Publishes nothing.
scripts.//publish-qualified-set: The owner's one action to publish every package with a retained qualification record that is not yet on the registry (issue #1227). Defaults to the same plan as publish:plan above; add --publish to run the owner-present publish loop, on the pinned release runtime, one interactive npm prompt per package. A failure in one package does not stop the rest -- see the script's own header for why this is an owner-present loop rather than a workflow_dispatch fan-out.
scripts.//check-conversation: Deliberately NOT part of `check` above. Every other check gate scans this checkout — offline, hermetic, exactly reproducible on a fork's CI run with no credentials. This one scans GitHub's live API instead: it needs network access and an authenticated `gh`, neither of which a fork's CI or an offline run has, so wiring it into `check` would make the whole chain fail (or silently no-op) for every contributor who isn't the repository owner. Run it separately, where those preconditions are actually met.
scripts.//check-package-visibility: Deliberately NOT part of `check` above, for the same reason as check:registry-parity: it calls the live public npm registry over the network, which no offline local `npm run check` run should be required to reach. It needs no credential at all in either direction it checks -- declared-package packument reads AND the scope roster read are both anonymous; see the script's own header for what that can and cannot distinguish, why it moved off GitHub Packages (issue #817), why the owner declined to store an NPM_PACKAGES_TOKEN for it, and why that decision did not by itself require cutting the roster-based check (only the separate retention cross-check was cut -- issue #844). Wired into CI as a scheduled run in package-visibility.yml.
scripts.//check-merge-policy: Deliberately NOT part of `check` above, for the same reason as check:conversation and check:package-visibility: it reads the live forge API and needs a token, so wiring it into the offline, hermetic `check` chain would fail it for every contributor who is not the repository owner. It compares the merge methods the forge offers for the default branch against governance/merge-policy.json and fails on drift. It is an OBSERVER, not an enforcer -- merge methods live in the forge settings store, not this tree, and writing them needs Administration-level access no gate here holds or should hold. It exists because GitHub composes a squash commit's message server-side and appends a Co-authored-by trailer built from an account's public profile email, which is how private identity reached this repository's commit messages with every git identity here already set to the noreply form. See the script's own header and SECURITY.md.
scripts.//check-registry-parity: Deliberately NOT part of `check` above because it calls a live registry. Public npmjs is verified anonymously down to packument SRI/shasum, served bytes, and packed manifest; the historical GitHub Packages lane still needs GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN. FAILS when a selected package version has no registry counterpart or its public artifact disagrees. Supports --package <directory> for bounded proof. See the script header.
scripts.//check-conversation-draft: The prevention mode: scan text BEFORE it is posted to an issue or PR, while withholding it is still free. Pass --file <path>, or pipe the draft text in: `echo "..." | npm run check:conversation:draft --`.
scripts.//check-shared-vocabularies: One vocabulary declared in two packages with no import between them (#443): controller/conventions LIVE_STATE_SURFACE_FINDING_KINDS and observer liveStateFindingKinds. The duplicate is deliberate — observer ships zero runtime dependencies on purpose, and builder’s collapse-into-a-re-export precedent explicitly relied on builder already depending on controller, which observer does not. So the copy stays and stops being unverified: observer’s own header said the two were “kept in sync by hand” with a code comment as the review step, and a reviewer noticing is not a mechanism. Compares SETS in both directions, never counts, because a renamed member keeps both counts equal — the drift most likely to actually happen. Runs after build (it imports both dist/ outputs) and reports the satisfied/violated/indeterminate ternary as 0/1/2, so an unbuilt or moved export is never reported as agreement.
scripts.//check-conflict-markers: An unresolved merge committed into a tracked file. Found the hard way: two files carried the three git conflict markers on main of this PUBLIC repository, through a full `npm run check` that passed, because nothing here looked for them. A sibling repository in this fleet has had a blocking gate for this for a while; this one did not. Note why the nearest gate could not help: check:readme is a PARITY check, comparing real exports against README table rows, and a conflict-marker line does not parse as a row -- so it is not a mismatch, it is nothing. Anchors all three marker forms to line start, requires the divider to be exactly seven equals AND to sit between an opener and a closer, so a Setext heading underline, a horizontal rule, and prose quoting the markers all stay clean. Scans the git tree rather than the working directory: a marker matters once it is committed, and a local in-progress merge is not this gate's business.
scripts.//verify-artifact-reproducible: Does this package's dist/ still reproduce? dist/ is gitignored, so every tree digest this repository computes is blind to it, and a qualification record is immutable -- a record bound to a tarball no clean build reproduces makes that version permanently unpublishable (issue #893). Deliberately NOT part of `check` above, and not because it is slow: it is DESTRUCTIVE, removing every packages/*/dist and rebuilding, which is the only honest way to answer. Deliberately NOT named check:* either, and this is the documented reason issue #414's rule asks for: on a CI runner the question is VACUOUS. A fresh runner has no pre-existing dist/, so what it packs is a clean build by construction and this command could only ever report a pass -- the exact shape of gate that proves nothing. The question is only meaningful on a machine with a working tree, which is where the binding it protects is created: generate-qualification-record.mjs runs the same assertion itself, with no opt-out, so the record path is closed whether or not anyone runs this by hand. Usage: npm run verify:artifact-reproducible -- packages/<name> [--tarball <candidate.tgz>].
scripts.//rehearse-publish-lifecycle: Execute the npm lifecycle scripts a publish would fire, in the environment the publish job runs in (issue #351). `npm publish --dry-run` does not run them and `--ignore-scripts` is passed deliberately on both sanctioned publish paths, so nothing else here has ever executed prepublishOnly -- which is a live gate for a hand-run `npm publish` (issue #273). Wired into publish.yml's qualify job; runnable directly against a package directory. Needs no credential and mutates no registry.
scripts.//check-qualification-deferral-issues: Deliberately NOT part of `check` above, for the same reason as check:merge-policy immediately above: it reads the live GitHub API and needs a token, so wiring it into the offline, hermetic `check` chain would fail it for every contributor who isn't the repository owner.
